draft.title: Magnetic fields
card: A magnetic field is the space around a magnet where its magnetic force acts. Another magnet or a piece of iron in this space feels a force.
We draw a magnetic field with field lines. Outside the magnet, the lines run from the north pole to the south pole. Arrows on the lines show this direction.
The field is strongest where the lines are closest together. This is near the poles. Far from the magnet the lines are spread out and the field is weaker.
Field lines are a model. They do not show real threads in the air. They help us show the direction and strength of the field.
draft.remember: Field lines run from north to south, and the closer they are, the stronger the field.

a.q: Field lines around a bar magnet are packed closely near its ends and spread out far away. What does this show?
opts: The field is stronger near the ends than far away
The field is weaker near the ends than far away
The field only exists where the lines are drawn
The field is the same strength everywhere
a.why: Lines that are close together show a strong field, so the field is strongest near the ends. The lines are a model, so the field is not limited to the places where lines are drawn.
a.clue: Think about what close lines mean.

b.q: Sam places a small compass near a bar magnet and moves it away. The compass needle reacts less and less. What best explains this?
opts: The magnet's field gets weaker further from the magnet
The magnet's field gets stronger further from the magnet
The magnet's field stops at the edge of the table
The compass needle runs out of magnetic force
b.why: The field is strongest close to the magnet, so the compass feels a smaller force as it moves away. The field does not get stronger with distance.
b.clue: Where are field lines closest together?

wants.brief: A bar magnet with its north pole (N) on the left and south pole (S) on the right. Field lines with arrows leave the north pole, curve around the outside and return into the south pole. The lines are closest together near the poles and spread out further away.
wants.why: It shows the direction of the lines and how their spacing shows the strength of the field.

a.best: The field is stronger near the ends than far away

b.best: The magnet's field gets weaker further from the magnet
